title: Long Inlet Time / No Water Fill
shortDescription: The dishwasher did not fill with water within the allowed time.
fullDescription: E1 on Hisense dishwashers (built-in and freestanding) means the controller has timed out waiting for the float or pressure switch to indicate sufficient water. Almost always caused by water supply issues, a clogged inlet filter, or a failed inlet valve.
symptoms: E1 displayed shortly after cycle start
Dry tub or only a small amount of water
No filling sound from the inlet valve

fixSteps.title: Check water supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the supply valve under the sink is fully open.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet filter
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the supply hose at the rear and clean the mesh screen at the inlet valve port.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hose
fixSteps.instruction: Look for kinks or crushed sections behind the unit and straighten.

fixSteps.title: Test inlet valve
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and measure resistance across the solenoid. Typical 800-1200 Ohm. Open or shorted = replace.

whenToCallPro: If the inlet valve is integrated into a complex assembly behind the toe-kick.

faq.q: Will it damage the heater if I keep retrying?
faq.a: No - a no-fill condition cancels the cycle before heating starts.

title: Long Drain / Drain Failure
shortDescription: The dishwasher did not pump out water within the expected time.
fullDescription: E2 indicates the drain pump ran but the float or pressure switch did not register an empty tub. Most commonly caused by a clogged filter, blocked drain hose, or failed drain pump.

causes.cause: Air gap or garbage disposal knockout plug not removed

symptoms: E2 with standing water in the tub
Drain motor humming with no water moving
Slow drain over multiple cycles before fault

fixSteps.title: Clean the filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the lower spray arm and the cylindrical filter at the sump. Rinse thoroughly under running water.

fixSteps.title: Inspect drain hose
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the unit out and check the drain hose for kinks or clogs. Use a wire to clear stubborn debris.

fixSteps.title: Check air gap / disposal plug
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the knockout plug was removed if connected to a new garbage disposal. Clean any air gap fitting.

fixSteps.title: Test drain pump
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and measure resistance. Typical ~30 Ohm. Replace if open or seized.

whenToCallPro: If you cannot pull the dishwasher out without disconnecting plumbing.

faq.q: Should I bail out the water first?
faq.a: Yes - removing standing water with a cup and towels makes filter access easier.

title: Heater Failure
shortDescription: Wash water did not reach target temperature.
fullDescription: E3 is logged when the dishwasher fails to heat the wash water to the expected temperature within the timeout. Either the heating element is open, the NTC is misreading, or the heater relay is failed.

causes.cause: Failed heater relay on main board

symptoms: E3 mid-cycle, dishes come out cold and dirty
Long cycle times before the fault
Detergent not fully dissolved

fixSteps.title: Test the heater
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the heating element terminals and measure resistance. Typical 15-30 Ohm. Open = replace.

fixSteps.title: Test NTC sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure NTC resistance at room temperature. Approximately 50 kOhm at 25 C is typical.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the integrated wash motor / heater module or NTC sensor as identified.

whenToCallPro: On flow-through heater designs the entire wash motor module must be replaced - often best done by a pro.

faq.q: Can I run cold cycles to delay repair?
faq.a: Cold cycles will not sanitize dishes - only suitable for very lightly soiled loads.

title: Anti-Flood / Overflow Detected
shortDescription: The base pan float switch has tripped indicating water in the base.
fullDescription: E4 indicates the base anti-flood float has detected water under the dishwasher. The drain pump runs continuously to clear the leak and the cycle is canceled until the float resets.

causes.cause: Leaking sump or wash motor seal
Tub leak from cracked weld or door gasket

symptoms: E4 with continuous drain pump running
Visible water under the unit
Water on the kitchen floor

fixSteps.title: Stop water supply
fixSteps.instruction: Close the supply valve to the dishwasher.

fixSteps.title: Locate leak source
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the unit out, place towels, and watch for the leak source during a fill test.

fixSteps.title: Repair connection or replace seal
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten or replace the inlet fitting; replace the wash motor seal kit if leaking from the bottom.

fixSteps.title: Dry the base
fixSteps.instruction: Tilt and dry the base pan to allow the float to return to its rest position before testing.

whenToCallPro: If the leak is from a cracked tub, repair is usually not cost-effective.

faq.q: Why is the pump still running?
faq.a: Hisense intentionally runs the drain pump while E4 is active to evacuate the leak.

title: Overfill Condition
shortDescription: The pressure switch reports water above the safe level.
fullDescription: E5 is set when the pressure (or flow) sensor reports water above the maximum fill level. Often due to a stuck-on inlet valve or a failed pressure switch.
symptoms: E5 with excess water in the tub
Splashing sounds even when paused
Cycle aborts shortly after start

fixSteps.title: Cancel and drain
fixSteps.instruction: Run a Cancel/Drain cycle to evacuate excess water.

fixSteps.title: Test the inlet valve
fixSteps.instruction: Close the supply valve and check whether water continues to enter; if so, the inlet valve is stuck open.

fixSteps.title: Replace inlet valve
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement valve, ensuring inlet filter is clean.

whenToCallPro: If the pressure switch tubing is integrated with the sump.

faq.q: Can I keep using the dishwasher?
faq.a: Stop using until the inlet valve is verified - water can keep entering even when off.

title: NTC Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The water temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: E6 reports a sensor fault on the NTC used for wash temperature feedback. The dishwasher cannot regulate heating safely and aborts the cycle.

causes.cause: Damaged wire from chafe at the door hinge

symptoms: E6 displayed early in cycle
Cycle aborts before any heating
Display temperature reads abnormally high or low

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the NTC harness at the wash motor or main board.

fixSteps.title: Test NTC
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and measure resistance. Approximately 50 kOhm at 25 C. Replace if out of range.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement sensor and route wiring away from heat-shrink seams.

whenToCallPro: If the NTC is integrated into the wash motor module.

faq.q: Will the dishwasher run cold cycles with E6?
faq.a: No - the controller blocks operation until the sensor reads valid.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: User interface and main control are not communicating.
fullDescription: E7 is shown when the touch panel does not receive valid serial messages from the main board. Cycle cannot start and existing cycle pauses.

causes.cause: Loose ribbon cable in the door hinge
Surge damage to the UI MCU

symptoms: E7 with no further response
Buttons do nothing
Door switch reads correctly but cycle will not start

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Trip the breaker for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open the inner door panel and reseat the ribbon between display and main board.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the user interface board first; if E7 persists, replace the main control.

whenToCallPro: If the main board needs to be replaced.

faq.q: Could a power surge cause this?
faq.a: Yes - surges damage the lower-voltage UI MCU first.

title: Diverter Motor Fault
shortDescription: The water diverter cannot reach the requested position.
fullDescription: Hisense dishwashers use a diverter to route water between upper and lower spray arms. E8 indicates the diverter motor is not turning, or the position sensor is not reporting correctly.

causes.cause: Debris jammed in the sump diverter

symptoms: E8 mid-cycle
Only the lower spray arm appears to run
Poor cleaning on the upper rack

fixSteps.title: Clean the sump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the filter and inspect the sump for glass shards, food, or labels jamming the diverter port.

fixSteps.title: Test diverter motor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the motor and measure resistance. Replace if open.

fixSteps.title: Replace diverter assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the diverter motor or full pump module per service sheet.

whenToCallPro: Most diverter repairs require partial disassembly of the wash motor module.

faq.a: No - but cleaning will be poor until resolved.

title: Wash Motor Fault
shortDescription: The circulation wash motor failed to start or stalled.
fullDescription: E9 indicates the main circulation pump (wash motor) failed to reach the commanded speed. Either the motor is jammed by debris, has failed windings, or the inverter on the main board failed.

causes.cause: Glass or debris in the impeller

symptoms: E9 within seconds of cycle start
Hum or click but no spray
Burnt smell from the base

fixSteps.title: Clean the sump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the filter and any debris that may be jamming the impeller.

fixSteps.title: Test motor windings
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the motor harness and measure each winding. Open or shorted = replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace wash motor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the wash motor assembly with the matching service part.

whenToCallPro: Wash motor replacement requires laying the dishwasher on its back - typically pro service.

faq.q: Should I replace or buy new?
faq.a: If the motor itself is failed, repair is comparable to half a new dishwasher - weigh the value.

title: Door Latch Switch Fault
shortDescription: The door is not registering as latched.
fullDescription: E0 is the door switch fault. The cycle will not start until the controller sees the latch switch closed. Often a broken latch hook or misaligned door.
symptoms: E0 when start is pressed
Loud rattle when closing the door
Cycle starts then aborts within seconds

fixSteps.title: Adjust latch alignment
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen the strike screw and adjust position until the door latches firmly.

fixSteps.title: Replace latch assembly
fixSteps.instruction: If a hook is broken, replace the latch board with the matching Hisense service part.

fixSteps.title: Test microswitch
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter to verify continuity changes when latch is engaged. Replace if stuck.

faq.q: Can I bypass the door switch?
faq.a: Never - the door switch is a safety device that prevents the cycle from running with the door open.
